summary.text: Democrat Justin Pearson, a Memphis state representative first elected in a 2023 special election, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Tennessee's 9th District to Brent Taylor.

A community organizer who co-founded an environmental advocacy group, he drew national attention in April 2023 when the Tennessee House voted to expel him after a gun-control protest on the House floor; the Shelby County Commission reinstated him days later, and he was re-elected in 2024.
He won the August 6, 2026 Democratic primary for the 9th District.

paragraphs.text: Pearson was born on January 7, 1995, in Memphis, according to the Tennessee General Assembly and Wikipedia, and his campaign says he is the fourth of five boys born to teenage parents.
His campaign website says that at age 15 he petitioned the school board to provide textbooks to his classmates.
He graduated from Mitchell High School in Memphis and from Bowdoin College in 2017, where Wikipedia reports he majored in Government & Legal Studies.
Pearson has worked as a community organizer and founded a nonprofit organization.
In 2020 he co-founded Memphis Community Against Pollution, one of the local groups involved in the effort that ended plans for the Byhalia Pipeline, according to Wikipedia.
The legislature lists among his honors the 2024 Truman Center Award for Exceptional Moral Courage in Public Service and the 2023 National Urban League Freedom Fighters Award.
The Shelby County Commission appointed Pearson acting state representative for District 86 on January 24, 2023, and he won the March 14, 2023 special election to formally take the seat.

On April 6, 2023, the Tennessee House voted 69–26 to expel him after he participated in a gun-control protest on the House floor, and the Shelby County Commission voted to reinstate him on April 12, 2023.
He won the August 3, 2023 special election with 94.0% of the vote and was re-elected in 2024.
Pearson announced his congressional campaign on October 8, 2025, and won the August 6, 2026 Democratic primary for the 9th District with 65.8% of the vote against three opponents.
He lives in Memphis with his wife, Oceana R. Gilliam-Pearson, according to his campaign website.
During the campaign, he emphasized affordability, Medicare for All, and holding data-center operators accountable.
He received 48.5% of the vote to Brent Taylor's 49.6%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
